rationale: Older adults who reported consuming oranges had lower unadjusted Rome III constipation prevalence, and one orange-pomace trial found higher stool frequency. This gives a minimal lean against worsening. The participant survey leaves preparation, confounding and symptom severity uncertain. A later pomace crossover and a small pasteurized-juice study were inconclusive. The evidence still lacks an isolated raw-orange comparison in Parkinson disease.

A small placebo-controlled fresh-sage-tip extract trial favored less menopausal fatigue. A dry-extract exhaustion comparison was inconclusive. Spanish-sage essential oil lowered some acute task-fatigue ratings in healthy volunteers. The minimal lean against worsening rests chiefly on the first trial and transfer from an extract and menopause to fresh culinary sage and Parkinson fatigue.

Oral olive-oil comparator trials used unspecified or refined oil and compared against other oil formulations. A topical extra-virgin oil thesis reports favorable within-arm sleep-quality scores. A population study reports favorable extra-virgin oil associations with global sleep quality. These sources leave insomnia severity after consuming extra-virgin olive oil in Parkinson disease unresolved.

The age-adjusted plasma ALA correlation favored less rigidity, with a weaker sex-adjusted result. A combined-regimen narrative described improvement. The two flaxseed omega-3 plus vitamin E trials give aggregate results and omit a separate rigidity estimate. The first trial’s registry changed dose and outcomes after publication. No contrast isolates cold-pressed flaxseed oil.

Isolated caffeine favored less Parkinson rest tremor at weeks three and six with intervals spanning zero. The trial used higher amounts than measured servings of black tea. Separate sources include worsening in some caffeine or coffee users, an acute oral caffeine test without clear worsening and tea cohorts with motor totals. The constituent link gives a minimal favorable lean for brewed black tea.

The aqueous spearmint trial’s two doses pointed in different directions for depression-dejection, with baseline imbalance and an inconclusive overall comparison. The blended extract trial was inconclusive. Peppermint extract reduced mouse tail-suspension immobility alongside motor recovery. The sources leave fresh spearmint and Parkinson depressive symptoms unresolved.
